allocation_complete.reason: The BMS-relevant aspect of the traction power limit (permitted discharge power) is covered by BMS_REQ_POWER_DERATING.

completeness.reason: The single obligation (limit delivered traction power to the product value) is addressed.

consistency.reason: Sibling BB_POWER_LIMITS states the vehicle traction power never exceeds the BMS discharge power AND the pack overcurrent limit, but this element only applies the derating; who keeps the vehicle below BMS_REQ_PACK_OVERCURRENT is not reconciled.
consistency.suggestion: Either have the power manager also respect the overcurrent limit (and allocate BMS_REQ_PACK_OVERCURRENT under bev) or narrow BB_POWER_LIMITS' wording to BMS-internal protection.

design_clarity.reason: The torque-domain cap is a concrete choice, but how the power limit is converted into a torque limit (speed-dependent P/omega, which speed signal) and how the BMS derating is combined (minimum of both) is left open.
design_clarity.suggestion: Specify torque_max = min(P_vehicle, P_BMS_derated) / motor speed (with the speed source and low-speed handling).

implementability.reason: A single bounded VCU function; the BEV-only derating input is resolved per product.

interface_only.reason: Sole allocates target BMS_REQ_POWER_DERATING is a BMS interface need (tag interface); the link is gated bev, matching where BMS needs exist.

no_value_copy.reason: The 55/60 degC derating values are not restated; only 'the power derating reported by the BMS'.

parent_fit.reason: Caps the torque request so delivered traction power stays within the vehicle limit, which is exactly REQ_TRACTION_POWER_LIMIT's obligation.

variant_consistency.reason: Ungated like REQ_TRACTION_POWER_LIMIT; the BMS link is a link variant <<bev: ...>> so it exists only where BMS needs exist.
